_about: Style rules for classifying FAA airport diagram (APD) vector objects. Data, not code: tools/airport_map/extract.py applies 'rules' in order (first match wins), then the geometry-dependent 'post' pass. Colours are the PAINTED fill/stroke colours (a colour left in the graphics state but not painted does not count). Lengths/areas are in PDF points after rotation to north-up.

rules.note: brown circles, label-box outlines and leaders
straight triangles (leader arrowheads); no glyph on an APD is a single straight triangle. Checked before glyph so a label box never absorbs a leader arrow
visible lettering is drawn as outlines over an invisible text layer; a small black fill inside a text label box is a letter
long thin black fill; length as a fraction of the frame's longer side (0.1: short runways at big airports, e.g. KBOS 15L/33R)
thin black bar drawn as a fill but too short for a runway (e.g. a blast fence)
post pass moves fills below post.building_min_area to symbol
dashed white centreline along each runway
white interiors of label boxes (HS 1/HS 2) and the cycle-date banners
small black fills: arrows, light symbols
strokes painted under a non-page clipping path (hatched areas)
closed shapes only: a long open line (e.g. a graticule parallel spanning the chart) is linework
leaders, taxiway centreline arcs, outlines; post pass finds graticule lines and ILS hold dashes

labels.note: graticule value printed as text, e.g. 37°40.0'N (KLGA prints them as outlines only: none in its text layer)
post pass splits into runway_end / elevation / gate_leadin (gate lead-in, keyed by gate number; Franco Oct 8: destination only, never a route element); leftovers stay 'number' and are listed
helipad designator (e.g. H1; NASR lists it as a runway/helipad), not a taxiway name
